section.name: Constant-pH Molecular Dynamics (CpHMD) with Force Field X (FFX)
section.p: This guide shows how to set up and run constant-pH simulations with FFX using the Ph* commands and titration utilities.

subsection.name: Overview
subsection.p: FFX supports constant-pH energy evaluation and dynamics on titratable sites. Core entry points:

ul.li: PhEnergy: evaluate energies for structures with titration states.
PhMinimize: minimize structures under CpH conditions.
test.SaveAsConstantPhPDB: write PDBs annotated for constant-pH workflows.
Utilities: see TitrationUtils and related code for protonation models.

subsection.p: See also the Ph* commands in the User Manual.

ol.li:
Start from a reasonable protonation state near your target pH.
Use Solvator --pH <value> during solvation to initialize states.
Ensure your .key selects an AMOEBA parameter set appropriate for your system (e.g., AMOEBA_BIO_2018).
Optionally, write a constant-pH annotated PDB for inspection:

subsection.name: Running CpHMD
subsection.p: Basic example at pH 7.0 using OpenMM engine, 100 ps:
subsection.source: ffxc PhDynamics \ --pH 7.0 \ --molecularDynamicsEngine OpenMM \ --integrator Verlet \ --thermostat Bussi \ --temperature 298.15 \ --dt 1.0 \ --numberOfSteps 100000 \ --report 0.5 \ --write 2.5 \ --checkpoint 5.0 \ --fileFormat XYZ \ input_cph.pdb

ul.li: --titrationModel, --titrationInterval, and related flags control how and how often titration state changes are proposed/accepted.
Use --npt <atm> with --isotropic or --anisotropic if pressure control is desired.
Equilibrate at fixed protonation first (standard Dynamics) before enabling CpH.
Start with shorter CpH intervals and gradually lengthen once stable.
Monitor titration states, pKa estimates, and ensure no persistent numerical instabilities.
Missing titratable assignments: check for proper residue naming and protonation states; consult TitrationUtils and logs.
Instability: decrease --dt, increase barostat/thermostat coupling times, or restrain highly mobile regions during equilibration.
